items.text: A CPQ Solution Built Into Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM

The Dynamics CPQ solution is a Configure, Price, Quote extension that lives inside the standard Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM Quote entity. It's built on Power Apps, with Azure Logic Apps handling the integrations back to cost sheets, vendor price lists, and downstream finance systems. Because it's scoped to ship alongside a Dynamics CRM implementation rather than as a follow-on project, quoting is available on the same record your sales team already works in from day one. Teams already comfortable building quotes in Excel typically pick up the grid without formal training, since the interaction is deliberately the same.

items.text: Quoting Complex Deals in Excel Isn't Working

In most Dynamics 365 CRM deployments, the opportunity record is where the sales team spends its day. Quoting tends to live somewhere else: a spreadsheet a rep copies from a previous deal, edits by hand, and sends over email. The disconnect between the CRM opportunity and the spreadsheet the customer actually sees is where the specific problems below tend to show up.
Broken formulas and manual re-keying

Every new quote typically starts as a copy of last quarter's file. A cell reference lands on the wrong row, or an inherited formula reads the wrong VAT rate, and the margin the customer signs turns out to be a percentage the finance team never approved. Nobody notices until the invoice.
No link back to the CRM opportunity

The spreadsheet ends up wherever the rep last saved it: a laptop, an email thread, sometimes a shared drive nobody else has been told about. The Dynamics opportunity has no idea the quote exists, so pipeline reporting keeps showing the state of the deal from before quoting started.
Nothing to audit when a margin is wrong

When a deal closes below target margin, there's rarely a trail. No record of who applied the discount, when, or against which underlying cost. Finance ends up reverse-engineering the quote from the invoice, which is slow, and usually inconclusive.
Roll-ups your team maintains by hand

In sales-ops teams we've worked with, someone spends the last week of every month adding up quotes across product categories, business units, and vendors. It's a job that exists only because the underlying data lives in files instead of in the CRM. When the mix shifts mid-month, the roll-up starts over.
No approval path before the price goes out

In the spreadsheet workflow, there's nothing sitting between an aggressive discount and the customer's inbox. Approval is an informal chat, and by the time a sales manager sees the numbers, the quote has usually already been sent.
The CPQ Solution Sits Inside the Standard Dynamics Quote

Open a Quote record in Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM. Alongside Summary, Details, and Related, there is a new tab: CPQ Lines. That tab is the entire solution. There's no separate application to install, no second login, and nothing to import back into the CRM after the quote is finished. The pricing grid, the roll-up totals, and the approval workflow all read and write against the same record your sales team already opens.

items.alt: CPQ Lines view showing multi-vendor product line items — LOB Division, Product OEM, Supplier, Microsoft SKUs, and description — as a native tab on the Dynamics 365 CRM Quote entity

items.text: The grid is deliberately Excel-shaped, because that's the interaction the sales team already has muscle memory for. Add lines, clear selected cells, paste values, save. The training curve is shorter than a from-scratch CPQ interface would be, and the reformatting risks that come with an actual spreadsheet aren't present because the underlying columns are typed and validated.
Two Views on Every Quote: Lines and Summary

Salespeople work in Lines while they build the quote. Finance and management review it in Summary. Both views read from one Dataverse record, so there's no export step and nothing to reconcile between the version sales is editing and the version management is approving.
What the Dynamics CPQ Solution Handles

The capabilities below cover the shape of quoting for multi-vendor, multi-currency deals. Every one of them maps to a Microsoft service you already run, so there's no new vendor infrastructure to procure, secure, or maintain.
Line-item pricing with cost, margin, and discount

Each line carries unit cost, total cost, recommended margin, discount percentage, and computed selling price. When any input changes, the totals recalculate in place, which is the responsiveness a salesperson expects from a spreadsheet but with typed columns and validation the spreadsheet doesn't have.
Multi-vendor line items with OEM and supplier

Every line records the OEM, the supplier, and whether the deal is being sold as an agent or as a principal. That structure exists because a typical reseller quote is rarely one vendor: it might be a Microsoft licensing line, a Ribbon SBC hardware line, and a services attachment, all on the same purchase order.
Automatic roll-up by category and business unit

The Summary view collapses hundreds of line items into a per-category, per-LOB, per-supplier view. Each row carries its own total cost, total selling price, and computed margin. Because the roll-up is derived from the same record as Lines, there's no monthly reconciliation and no side calculations to keep in sync.
Multi-currency and VAT-aware totals

Currency is set on the quote and the CPQ solution handles the local tax posture from there. VAT, discount, shipping, and admin fees roll into the final selling price the customer sees, so the multi-currency work isn't handled after the fact by a separate finance calculation.
Discount categories and performance obligations

Each line carries a discount category and a performance-obligation description. That makes revenue-recognition and stand-alone selling price (SSP) reporting derivable directly from the quote data, rather than being reconstructed by finance after close. For teams operating under IFRS 15, this is the shape the standard actually asks for.
Native tab on the Quote entity — not a bolt-on

The CPQ Lines tab sits alongside Summary, Details, and Related on the standard Dynamics 365 Quote form. There's no context switching, no separate login, and no export back to the CRM at the end. Sales, management, and finance all look at the same record, which is what removes most of the classic "whose number is right" arguments.
Built on Power Apps, Logic Apps, and Dataverse

Nothing in this CPQ solution introduces new vendor infrastructure. It's Microsoft cloud from the pricing grid down to the identity layer, which matters for organizations whose IT team already has an established operating model for Microsoft services and doesn't want a second one.
Power Apps for the pricing grid

The Excel-familiar CPQ Lines and Summary views are a Power App embedded on the Dynamics Quote form. Anything a Power App can do (validation rules, computed columns, custom controls) is available for extension later without pulling in a new toolchain.
Logic Apps for integration

Cost sheets, vendor price lists, discount matrices, and downstream systems like ERP and finance are wired in through Azure Logic Apps. Each connector is a first-class Microsoft artifact your team can monitor, secure, and modify with the tooling they already use for other Azure workloads.
Dataverse for storage

CPQ data lives in Dataverse alongside the rest of your Dynamics 365 CRM records. Same tenant, same region, same backup and retention policies. There's no shadow database sitting on someone's laptop or in a vendor cloud you'd have to reason about separately.
Azure Active Directory for identity

Users sign in with the Azure Active Directory credentials they already use for Outlook, Teams, and Dynamics itself. Conditional access, multi-factor authentication, and role-based access controls apply automatically, because there isn't a second identity system to configure.

items.text: The Right Fit for Teams Already in the Microsoft Ecosystem

This solution is opinionated about who it works well for. The strongest fit is a company that has already committed to Dynamics 365 as the system of record for sales, and where project operations or accounting are running on the same platform, so the numbers on the quote have somewhere useful to flow after the deal closes. It fits less well as a standalone quoting tool bolted onto a CRM you're not otherwise invested in. If Salesforce is your CRM of record, a Salesforce-native CPQ is almost certainly the better answer.
IT resellers and distributors

A reseller's quote is rarely one vendor. The multi-vendor line detail (OEM, supplier, agent-versus-principal treatment) and the per-line performance-obligation field are built for the mix a typical reseller PO actually carries: licensing from one manufacturer, hardware from another, and services attached to both.
Services companies on Dynamics 365 Project Operations

If your delivery team is already running in Dynamics 365 Project Operations, quoting on the same platform means the sold price and the project scope arrive at delivery on the same record. No hand-off between systems, and no re-keying between the sales world and the delivery world.
Teams moving off spreadsheet-based quoting

For teams whose current quoting process is a shared Excel template, the switching cost is mostly about data model rather than user experience. The grid interaction is the same, so the muscle memory transfers. What changes is where the record actually lives, which is the point of the move.
Delivered With Your Microsoft CRM Implementation
Ships with the CRM rollout

The CPQ solution is scoped, configured, and deployed as part of the Dynamics 365 CRM implementation project, rather than as a separate engagement six months later. In practice, that means the sales team has quoting available in the CRM from the day the CRM itself goes live.
Delivered by a Microsoft Solutions Partner

Folio3 is a Microsoft Solutions Partner and supports this CPQ solution alongside our Dynamics 365, Business Central, Azure, and Power Platform work. One delivery team, one support relationship, and the same account owner across the surrounding Microsoft stack.
Extensible with Power Platform

New columns, alternate approval flows, additional integrations, and custom validation rules are built with the same Power Apps and Power Automate tooling your team already uses on other Microsoft applications. No specialist toolchain, and no separate certification for admins.
Local tax, currency, and compliance

VAT handling, multi-currency posture, and regional compliance rules are configured to match the markets your business actually operates in, rather than shoehorned into a generic template that assumes a single home country.
Analytics on the roadmap

Charts, dashboards, and margin visualization over quote data are planned as a follow-on phase, built with Power BI on top of the same Dataverse tables. The data model already carries the fields the analytics work will need, so this is a delivery order decision rather than a re-architecture.
